_comment: Shared vectors for panel template instantiation (protocol 3.0, docs/lwf/formats/panels.md).
Each case: `template` ({views, blocks}) instantiated against `views` (each view's data by view name)
must deep-equal `expect`. Every client implementation runs this table: `instantiate` in
loreweaver-protocol/v3 does (panels.test.ts), and the server checks its condition evaluator

cases.why: nothing to resolve, nothing to hide: a divider always survives
the ordinary bound gauge: value and bounds read from a built-in view
a module view is read under the handle the panel declared for it
a view the client does not hold is absent: the block bound to it is not drawn, its neighbours are
a path that names nothing in the view is a miss, and a miss in a required field drops the block
a path may only start with a handle the template declares
records by property, lists by index or by key — `id`, then `key`
an index the list does not reach resolves to nothing
a field bound to a list or a record has nothing to show
a zero-width gauge cannot be drawn, so it is not sent
a gauge bound to text resolves to nothing, never to a guess
a stat's value keeps its TYPE: 7 is not '7' and true is not 'true'
JavaScript's String(): one number type and lowercase booleans
a label is required — a stat with a value and no name says nothing
the happy path for the optional enum, bound
optional enums: drop the field, keep the block
`style` is authored, not bound
content-addressed; caption and alt are ordinary text fields
a hashless picture would be a dead fetch
caption/alt are optional: the picture still ships
each option runs a command, as the viewer, with its arguments
an option whose label misses, or with no command, goes alone
an empty chooser is worse than no chooser
the four performance templates with every field
a letter with no body is not a letter
the block still performs, one line shorter
fractions of the map's own box: a pin outside it is clamped, not dropped
a pin with nowhere to sit is not a pin
an admin's view flags what players do not see; a panel cannot read it, by key or by index
the same rule from the other side: hidden elements are removed before anything
the element is read under the repeat's `as` handle
inside a repeat the declared handles stay in scope
`prefix` keeps the elements whose key starts with it — the way to walk one branch of the variable tree
MAX_REPEAT_INSTANCES is 32: 35 elements expand to exactly 32, in order
the cap is on instances after the prefix filter, not on how deep a match sits
a repeat over a record or a scalar expands to nothing
a repeat inside a repeat resolves to nothing at all — the build refuses it too
the author gating the WHOLE list: false hides every instance
a gate on the inner block decides each instance on its own
the value gate a missing binding cannot express
ordering text against a number is an error; an error HIDES, never shows
the build refuses an empty or non-text condition; a hand-made one hides
a view not held reads as null: a gate against it is undecidable or false, never shown by accident
a condition sees scalars only: a list or record is whether it holds anything
a condition cannot see a hidden element either
MAX_BINDING_PATH_DEPTH is 8 parts
no empty segment, no leading zero, no inherited property
MAX_PANEL_BLOCKS is 32: a template of 33 blocks is refused whole, never cut
a block kind this version does not know is not drawn
